statement: Justeson, John S., and Terrence Kaufman ("A Decipherment of Epi-Olmec Hieroglyphic Writing," Science 259(5102), 1993, pp. 1703-1711) claimed a decipherment of La Mojarra Stela 1 identifying the underlying language as pre-proto-Zoquean. Houston, Stephen D., and Michael D. Coe ("Has Isthmian Writing Been Deciphered?" Mexicon 25, 2003, pp. 151-161) argue Justeson and Kaufman imposed Mayan grammatical/spelling assumptions onto Epi-Olmec signs, and that the system failed an independent test when applied to a Teotihuacan-style Isthmian-script mask. Andrew Robinson's Lost Languages (2008 ed.) summarizes the field's state as "decidedly unproven." Justeson and Kaufman have continued defending and refining the decipherment — this remains an active, unresolved two-camp dispute, not a settled decipherment.
scholarly_disagreement: Justeson and Kaufman [DECIPHERMENT-CLAIM SCHOOL] maintain the pre-proto-Zoquean reading; Houston and Coe [SKEPTICAL SCHOOL] argue the method imposed Mayan assumptions and failed an independent test.

interpretations.position: Epi-Olmec script has been deciphered; underlying language is pre-proto-Zoquean
interpretations.strongest_case: A internally consistent reading of La Mojarra Stela 1 and the Tuxtla Statuette against a reconstructed pre-proto-Zoquean grammar, defended and refined against later challenges.

interpretations.position: The claimed decipherment is unproven; the method imposed external (Mayan) grammatical assumptions and failed independent testing
interpretations.strongest_case: Applying the Justeson-Kaufman system to an independent Isthmian-script object (a Teotihuacan-style mask) did not produce a coherent parse.
